subject: Tenor conversion & uptake roadmap (co-term + auto-renew options)
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@brightwell.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning & structure options for FY27

Hi Camila,

We're starting the renewal conversation for our Redwood deployment (account BW-2345). Usage has been trending up — attached is our Q4 export. Our procurement and finance teams want to evaluate two paths: (A) lock a multi-year committed term with an annualized ramp and co-term to our fiscal year, or (B) convert to a usage-first model with a predictable minimum and an option to auto-renew.

Key asks from our side:
- Pricing guidance for both multi-year and convert-to-usage structures (including any credits for co-term).
- A suggested ramp schedule (months 1-6) for a staged capacity increase and a burst safety clause.
- How auto-renew would work operationally and if there's an early opt-out clause.

We're on a tight timeline — our board wants a proposal by next Thursday (2026-12-09). Can you outline options and include a draft SOW/amendment?

Thanks,
Ethan Ross
SaaS Operations, Brightwell Health
attachments: usage_report_Q4.csv
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@brightwell.com>
Cc: Ava Lund <ava.lund@brightwell.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & structure options for FY27

Hi Ethan / Ava,

Thanks — got the report and appreciate the clear asks. I put together two concrete options below and attached a draft SOW (Brightwell_SOW_v3.pdf) plus a one-pager that maps costs across the first 12 months. High-level: both paths are achievable; trade-offs are predictability vs flexibility.

Option A — Multi-year, co-term (Recommended if budget predictability is priority):
- 3-year term (co-term to Brightwell FY) with year-over-year staged ramp: Year1 40%, Year2 70%, Year3 100% of committed capacity.
- Early ramp credits: if usage in months 1-6 exceeds the staged threshold, we apply a one-time credit to month 7 invoice to smooth costs.
- SLA: priority routing and 99.9% availability SLA in Dedicated pool.

Option B — Convert-to-usage with minimum and auto-renew (Recommended if flexibility is priority):
- Usage-first billing with a 12-month minimum spend floor (can be expressed as a monthly minimum).
- Optional auto-renew on 30-day notice; early opt-out with 60-day termination fee equal to 1x monthly minimum.
- We recommend a 3-month pilot pricing for burst capacity followed by a standard usage tier.

Ramp schedule proposal (both options):
- Month 0 (sign): onboarding + 25% reserved capacity for pilot.
- Months 1-3: linear ramp to 50% of target capacity.
- Months 4-6: linear ramp to 80-100% depending on choice.
- Burst clause: allow 30% re-routable burst for up to 10 days per quarter at a pre-agreed rate.

Commercial levers we can offer: co-term credit (one-time), frontloaded onboarding credit, and a conversion credit if you convert to multi-year within 90 days of pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll circulate a short internal pricing note and proposed amendment language (today).
2) If the structure looks OK, we'll send a formal pricing table + SOW for signature by 12/09.

Attaching: Brightwell_SOW_v3.pdf (draft), cost_one_pager.pdf

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: Renewal planning & structure options for FY27 — pricing + amendment input

Team —
Forwarding Brightwell's asks (below). They want a decision window by 12/09. Can we align on two priced scenarios (3yr co-term + convert-to-usage with min) and confirm the ramp and burst terms? Things to confirm:
- Co-term credit sizing (what's reasonable to offer for an FY co-term alignment).
- Pilot frontload credit amount for the 3-month pilot.
- Any recommended language for auto-renew + opt-out (legal prefers specific notice windows).

Marissa — can you draft the amendment language for a 3yr co-term and the alternate convert-to-usage amendment?
Karthik — can you run model pricing and show net ARR impact across 3 years vs usage conversion?
Jonas — ops: confirm we can commit to the burst clause and what telemetry we need to instrument the ramp.

I'll keep Ethan and Ava updated after we sync.

-Camila
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal planning & structure options for FY27 — pricing + amendment input

Camila / team,

Quick modeling notes (high level):
- Multi-year (3yr) co-term: recommend a 12% effective credit across committed spend to account for co-term and multi-year commitment. That gets us to an attractive net price while preserving gross ARR.
- Convert-to-usage with 12-month minimum: recommend a 7% conversion credit applied to the first 12 months' invoices and a monthly minimum equal to ~60% of Year1 expected spend.
- Pilot credit: offer a one-time $25k onboarding credit if they commit to a pilot that moves to a paid model within 90 days.

Operational constraints:
- Burst: we can support the 30% burst for a limited window but need to implement a short-term quota override and alerting to avoid overload; Ops will need ~2 weeks lead time to pre-provision.
- Auto-renew: legal prefers 30-day renewal notice with a 60-day opt-out termination fee window.

I'll produce a table comparing NPV/ARR impacts for both options by EOD and include recommended amendment language bullets for Marissa to convert into SOW text.

-karthik
From: Ava Lund <ava.lund@brightwell.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@brightwell.com>
Cc: procurement@brightwell.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Decision: Proceed with 3yr co-term + optional auto-renew upgrade

Camila / team,

Thank you for the options and the quick modeling. After internal review we are inclined to proceed with Option A (3-year co-term) with the following specifics:
- 3-year co-term, co-terminus with Brightwell FY starting 2027-01-01.
- Year1 commit at 45% of forecasted target with the ramp schedule you proposed (onboarding + 25% pilot; months 1-3 to 50%, months 4-6 to 80%).
- Accept the 12% effective credit for co-term and the $25k onboarding credit.
- Include the burst clause as discussed (30% for up to 10 days per quarter).
- Add auto-renew as an optional addendum: Brightwell can elect auto-renew with 30-day notice; if exercised, we request a 60-day opt-out fee window.

Please send the formal amendment and SOW for signatures (DocuSign link preferred). Also include the pre-provisioning timeline for Ops so we can align internal stakeholders.

Best,
Ava Lund
CFO, Brightwell Health
